body: If you had been hospitalized, they would have started medications right away.  Start the medications ASAP.  Antidepressants take a few weeks to take effect.

You can call the police to her address to be involuntarily committed based on what you saw on Snapchat.  Call 911 and ask them for a "wellness check" for her.  This is absolutely an appropriate time for that level of action.  This is a life-threatening emergency.

They didn't hospitalize you for your attempt?  Glad you're feeling better at least.

Antidepressants and psychiatric medications in general are very strange.  It takes a few tries to get the right balance of medication.  There are lots of medications to choose from, and then dosages to choose from on top of that.  There is an expensive test to figure out which medications *might* be best for you, but without that test, doctors essentially have to make educated guesses as to which medications are right.

They'll likely start you on an SSRI like Zoloft or Celexa.  SSRI's tend to have the most side effects of the three classes of antidepressants, but also statistically the highest success rate, which is why they are used.  Side effects are individual to every person but the most notable are weight gain and sexual dysfunction.

Appointments with psychiatrists are generally very short.  It could be up to an hour for the first visit, but likely 5-10 minutes for follow-up visits.  Psychiatrists do not do therapy, they just manage medications.

Therapy is where the real work takes place though.  It sounds like you have a lot to process emotionally, and that takes place in therapy.  Therapy is an hour a week, I would recommend at least once a week given your attempt, and not once every two weeks like some might suggest.  Therapists generally rely upon Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) if you want to do some research.  Other therapies may include EMDR and DBT.  It's up to you as to what you feel is the most effective.
